name: West Greenlandic Eskimo Pidgin
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.citation: van der Voort, Hein. 2013. Eskimo Pidgin. Survey chapter, APiCS Online (= The Survey of Pidgin and Creole Languages, vol. 3, 166–173, OUP). https://apics-online.info/surveys/76
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Section 4 Phonology deals with the Herschel Island Trade Jargon (glottocode eski1266), not the West Greenlandic pidgin; it says only that Stefánsson (1909), following Powell's manual, 'indicates stress by an apostrophe following the stressed syllable' (e.g. sī'-la 'weather') and that 'In Eskimo proper, phoneme length and stress are unrelated, and the notation of length in the Pidgin sources seems independent of stress notation too'. No statement of where stress falls, and nothing on stress for the West Greenlandic variety (which appears only in Table 5 and the text sample).

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Mentions loss of r and q and of sh/clusters (orsoq > oksok; nigsik > nieksik); nothing on stress.

sources.citation: APiCS Online, contribution 76 'Eskimo Pidgin' structure dataset (van der Voort 2013) and APiCS feature list (CLDF)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: APiCS has no word-stress feature (the only suprasegmental feature is 120 Tone); the language row gives glottocode eski1266 and states the default lect is the Herschel Island Trade Jargon, so the dataset does not describe west2864.

sources.citation: Petersen, Robert & Rischel, Jørgen. 1985. Sproglig indledning og kommentar til Resens tysk-grønlandske ordliste. Tidsskriftet Grønland 1985(5): 156–171.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Section 'Hvad fortæller ordlisterne os om udtalen af grønlandsk i ældre tid' (pp. 165–171) discusses vowels, diphthongs ai/au and consonants of 17th-century Greenlandic as reflected in Resen's 1687 wordlist; it calls a few items (Iliout, Panningina) 'en slags »pidgin-grønlandsk«' (p. 164) but says nothing about stress or accent (no 'tryk'/'betoning'/'accent' in the text).

sources.citation: Rischel, Jørgen & Petersen, Robert. 1985. Resens tysk-grønlandske ordliste. Tidsskriftet Grønland 1985(5): 172–192.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Edited German–Greenlandic wordlist of 1687 with modern Kalaallisut identifications; notes 'Uvanga Nulia var »pidgin«-grønlandsk' for the entry 'my wife'; nothing on stress.

sources.note: The only dedicated (102-page) description of the West Greenlandic pidgin, built from the 17th–18th-c. wordlists; if anything is said about accent marks in the old sources (e.g. kóna, konâ) or about pidgin prosody, it is here. Glottolog 5.3 attaches it to west2864 (ref 133506).
